newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche BA ups flights, sees 98-99 profit.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche BA ups flights, sees 98-99 profit.

text.p: Deutsche BA expects to increase turnover 22 percent to 600 million marks in the April 1996-March 1997 fiscal year with a 14 percent rise in passengers to 2.5 million, Carl Michel, DBA managing director from April 1 told Reuters.

"Our seat load factors will still be mid-50s and we need high 50s to break even. 1998-99 is the year when we expect to make a small profit which means we expect to break even in about 18 months' time," he said in an interview at this week's ITB travel show in Berlin.
DBA, a British Airways unit, will also increase seat capacity between Munich and Duesseldorf by 37 percent from March 30 as part of a new strategy to break even within 18 months, he said.

It will upgrade to 11 from eight daily flights in competition with 14 Lufthansa services. But it will maintain eight daily flights on all other Germany routes apart from the six times a day Berlin-Stuttgart service, he added.
Michel said the airline would in future add frequencies to existing routes rather than increase destinations in order to seize market share from Deutsche Lufthansa AG in its home market.

DBA would only compete with Lufthansa if it had at least 40 percent of route capacity and had thus decided not to fly Frankfurt-Berlin since it had been awarded only four of the 20 slots for flights between the two cities, Michel noted.
"If there are 20 frequencies we have got to be flying at least eight of them," he said.

But the airline now flew seven of the top 11 German domestic routes in competition to Lufthansa after starting Munich to Hamburg and to Cologne in January and was only missing four Frankfurt routes, he added.

Michel said DBA fares tended to undercut Lufthansa by 10-15 percent, adding that up to 98 percent of flights left within 15 minutes of scheduled departure compared to a published Lufthansa average "in the 80s".

Maintenance of full commission payments for travel agents, a new dedicated sales force, the launch of electronic ticketing and improved services for frequent flyers were other key elements under the new management team, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
